Write the complex number $z$, shown on the Argand diagram above, in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =3+2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & ≈0.588.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =0.588$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{0.588\,\text{i}}.
$$
